newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa grants amnesty to police hit squad trio.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa grants amnesty to police hit squad trio.

text.p: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission said on Monday it had granted amnesty to a former police hit squad leader and two cohorts for the killing of an anti-apartheid lawyer.
The trio were convicted of murdering attorney Griffiths Mxenge in a High Court trial earlier this year. The trial was suspended pending the outcome of the amnesty hearing.
Dirk Coetzee, the former commander of a covert police assassination squad, and his black accomplices David Tshikalange and Almond Nofomela, will not now be sentenced.
The truth commission's amnesty committee said in a statement their request was granted on the grounds that they had acted on the orders of senior security police officers.

"We are satisfied that they did what they did because they regarded it as their duty as policemen who were engaged in the struggle against the African National Congress and other liberation movements," the committee added.

The truth commission has powers to grant amnesty to those who committed political crimes during apartheid. The aim is to encourage perpetrators to come forward with the full truth and to promote reconciliation.
